status: Draft FHGM conformance suite, prepared from the reviewed model contract. FHGM has no released contract, no schemaVersion, no schema URL and no schemas/versions.json entry, and selection rule V7 keeps it that way until the shared publication PR lands; nothing here publishes, adopts or claims support. Expectations are derived from clauses, including independent accepted promotion records. Actual checker observations are reported separately by run_conformance.py against exact registered base bytes.
baseSchema: provenance.json records the two released FHGFF3 base bytes this suite evaluates: the 1.1 (v0.5.0) release every sealed expectation below was observed against - the record lane - and the 1.2 (v0.6.0) release under which base_matrix.json re-observes identity-rewritten twins (maintainer dual-base decision 2026-11-15; base selection, not substitution: no expectation or vector byte below is repointed). run_conformance.py verifies those bytes, the base-schemas.json registry the checker reads and the recorded contract and generator artifacts before it reports anything.
ruleVocabulary: K1-K6 are the FHGM model-level rules and B1 the boundary above them; they are drafted in this repository and are not registered in the shared conformance manifest, whose R1-R15, M, J, P, G and V namespaces keep their meanings. Vectors may also cite shared rules (sharedRules) where the shared text is the authority. The shared suite enumerates released types only, so this manifest is the seed the #204 publication PR either absorbs into conformance/manifest.json under ids it chooses, or mirrors with a cross-repository digest check - see README.md.
contextVocabulary: Pointer resolution is context-dependent: `context.predecessors` names the prior snapshots handed to the checker, in addition to the vector's own bytes. Two entries may therefore share one file and differ only in the history supplied - that pair is how deviation D3's bound is pinned.
layers: Each vector records what four independent checks report: base (the released fhgff3.json schema alone, over the parsed header), checksum (verify when the file-bound SHA-512/256 covers the bytes, stale when the header states a digest the bytes no longer produce), gff3 (gff3-validate --no-header over the feature layer, a separate tool: each vector records its own outcome, including the bare-Parent syntax rejection) and model (the draft checker's outcome). These observations bind to the v0.5.0 base bytes; the checker is handed both registered base releases and prints, for every loaded file, the release it selected from that file's cited schema URL, so no verdict is silent about which bytes produced it. The checksum field always holds the value the file states, stale or not, so a tampered vector pins which digest it kept. An invalid vector records the reason substring the checker must print. A reader without gff3-validate reports that layer as skipped; no FHGM rule depends on it.

K1.summary: Transport: an FHGM-carrying file keeps a released FHGFF3 identity - the v0.5.0 citation with schemaVersion 1.1, or the v0.6.0 citation with schemaVersion 1.2 or 1.1 (maintainer dual-base decision 2026-11-15; each citation may use the w3id URL or the raw tag URL under either repository name) - and carries one or more records under the single top-level x-fhgm-models key (docs/FORMAT.md R15). The checker validates the file against the registered base release its schema URL cites and refuses a citation no registered release answers to (raw main, superseded releases) or whose bytes were not supplied. A file stating FHGFF3 1.0 cannot carry the extension at all.

K2.summary: Record shape: every record validates against the native record contract, whose required set is modelId, modelVersion, featureId and reference (deviation D1); nested objects are closed; opaque text values are non-empty, carry no leading or trailing whitespace and no control, zero-width or bidirectional formatting character; link fields (evidence uri, software uri, methods protocol) must be URIs with a scheme the shared FORMAT.md R14 accepts.

K3.summary: modelId is unique within one annotation snapshot, compared after Unicode NFC normalisation, and checked before any per-record rule. A duplicate makes the identity a pointer needs unselectable, reported under the name ambiguous, and rejects that snapshot (checker rule 1, deviation D4).

K4.summary: featureId resolves, percent-decoded, to exactly one local root gene row (type gene or SO:0000704, with no Parent attribute) in the enclosing file (checker rule 2).

K5.summary: A record reference shares at least one comparable form with the file genome link and never contradicts it (checker rule 3). Both halves are enforced, which is stricter than the adoption packet's D1 summary; the maintainers confirm that strength.

K6.summary: A predecessor pointer resolves against explicitly supplied prior snapshots only: it names its own modelId (deviation D2), the recorded version differs, the assembly link and record reference match, and a recorded successor present in the supplied set is not skipped (checker rule 4, deviation D3).

R3.summary: Shared checksum rule 3, cited rather than redefined: the file checksum excludes the root checksum line and its terminator and covers every other byte, so it covers the embedded record bytes.

R15.summary: Shared extension rule, cited rather than redefined: a top-level x- key is admitted from FHR 2.1 and FHP and FHGFF3 1.1; any other unknown key and any x- key inside a nested object stays invalid.

B1.summary: Boundary, not a model rule: a file must already satisfy the released FHGFF3 base schema and its exact-byte checksum before any FHGM verdict exists. Model checks add to those guarantees and never replace them, so a rejection reported under B1 is not evidence of a model-level gap.

O2.summary: Split and merge of models across records.

O3.summary: Assembly migration of a model between references.

O5.summary: Who may mint an external model identifier.
O5.vectors: supplied-external-model-id admits a supplied value; it authorises nothing

O6.summary: Whether a supplied snapshot with an unresolved own pointer may serve as history.
O6.decision: raised as #204 Q7 on 2026-11-14; v0.x says yes
O6.vectors: history-with-unresolved-own-pointer pins behavior, not a ruling

O7.decision: #204 D4 review of 2026-11-14: snapshot level only in v0.x

O8.decision: separate decision with its own evidence, outside the header check

vectors.reason: does not match '^(?:(?:[Hh][Tt][Tt][Pp][Ss]?
vectors.description: K2 link fields (evidence uri, software uri, methods protocol) accept only the schemes the shared FORMAT.md R14 accepts: http, https or ftp with a host, or urn:, doi: or info:. javascript:void(0) is a well-formed URI that no renderer should link, so this draft record contract rejects it where the released header types only warn.

vectors.reason: is not a 'uri'
vectors.description: K2 enforces format: uri, not only the accepted scheme: the evidence URI has an https scheme and host but contains a space, which no URI may contain.

vectors.reason: 'https://user@/' does not match
vectors.description: K2 link fields accept http, https or ftp only with a host. In https://user@/ the authority is user information followed by an empty host (urlsplit hostname is None); format uri accepts the value, so only the link pattern's host check rejects it.

vectors.reason: 'ftp://user@/' does not match
vectors.description: K2 host check on the methods protocol, ftp scheme: ftp://user@/ names a user but no host. format uri accepts it; the link pattern rejects it.

vectors.reason: 'https://@/' does not match

vectors.reason: Additional properties are not allowed

vectors.reason: 'reference' is a required property

evidenceSemantics: layers.model retains the historical checker-process outcome. evidenceExpectation.model is earned fullModel evidence; not-run cannot count as rejection or pass. Actual rule/layer receipts are emitted by --report-json.

K3: all carrier model records after K2
K4: complete trustworthy local carrier feature inventory (ID/type/Parent presence)
K6: explicitly supplied prior snapshots with relevant K1-K5 prerequisites, including complete trustworthy feature inventories
recorded successor relations within supplied history only

fullModelRequirements: All selected-file K1-K6 predicates and relevant supplied-snapshot prerequisites must pass. Focus labels are not dependency declarations. No feature inventory means K4 not-run, not pass; known complete empty inventory rejects K4. No external or transitive history service.
